test_modes.name: MPC training/feature modes
test_modes.purpose: Exercise DFE, Vref, ZQ, and read/write training.

test_modes.name: Connectivity / boundary test
test_modes.purpose: Verify the CA / DQ / DQS / CK wiring on the module.

test_modes.name: Loopback / write-read
test_modes.purpose: Functional verification of the data path per sub-channel.

spec_provided_observability.name: Mode Register Read (MRR)
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Read configuration and status registers, including on-die-ECC error counts and ECS results.

spec_provided_observability.name: On-die ECC error reporting
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Single-bit error counts and Error Check and Scrub (ECS) status via mode registers.

spec_provided_observability.name: ALERT_n
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Signals write-CRC and command/address parity errors to the controller.

spec_provided_observability.name: Training feedback (MPC)
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Read training results (DFE taps, VrefDQ/VrefCA centers, read/write deskew).

spec_provided_observability.name: ZQ calibration status
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Output-driver / ODT calibration against the ZQ reference resistor.

no_jtag_on_DRAM_balls: LPDDR5 SDRAM has no JTAG / boundary-scan pins at the package interface; vendor DFT runs at wafer probe.
controller_side_debug_aids: Logic-analyzer / oscilloscope probing of CK / WCK / RDQS / CA[6:0] / CS / DQ / DMI.
LPDDR5 PHY / controller IPs expose FIFOs, WCK2CK leveling state, per-bit deskew, eye-margin sweeps, DFE taps via a vendor control register interface.
RDCAL fixed pattern as a deterministic read self-test.
Link-ECC error counters and controller-side system ECC.
notes: DDR5's protocol-level test/debug surface is the mode registers (MRR/MRW), on-die-ECC error reporting and ECS, ALERT_n for write-CRC and CA-parity errors, ZQ calibration, and MPC-driven training feedback. Chip-level JTAG/scan/BIST remain vendor / DRAM-die concerns; conformance is established by JEDEC compliance testing.
stacked_die_test_strategy: HBM3 test is hierarchical: each DRAM die is screened; the stack is tested as a known-good-stacked-die (KGSD) through the base die's IEEE-1500 / direct-access ports; the stack-on-interposer is tested for TSV / microbump integrity. TSMC produces the base die for HBM and is a foundry for HBM stacking.
error_detection_mechanisms: On-die ECC corrects single-bit errors inside the die.
Error Check and Scrub (ECS) scrubs accumulated single-bit errors.

interrupt_or_event_sources.trigger: A single-bit error is corrected; the count is readable via MRR.
